# Cisco IOS / IOS-XE — GUI ↔ CLI ↔ SNMP Mapping

Per [`gui-cli-snmp-unification.md`](../../00-architecture/gui-cli-snmp-unification.md): the CLI column is the literal, multi-line command text that must be echoed into the terminal exactly as a human would type it (including entering/exiting the required mode context) — not a paraphrase. Where no SNMP SET path exists, that's stated plainly rather than inventing one; per the architecture doc, SignalScope must never assume a fallback exists.

| GUI Action | CLI as echoed in terminal | SNMP SET (MIB::object, OID) | Read-back / GUI sync source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable port | `configure terminal`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/1`<br>`no shutdown`<br>`end` | `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus.<ifIndex> = up(1)` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7`) | `IF-MIB::ifOperStatus` (SNMP GET) or `show interfaces GigabitEthernet0/1 status` | Both CLI and SNMP paths are reliable on Cisco. SNMP is the correct fallback only when no live CLI session is open; per the unification doc, prefer CLI when a session exists. |
| Disable port | `configure terminal`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/1`<br>`shutdown`<br>`end` | `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus.<ifIndex> = down(2)` | Same as above | |
| Set port description | `configure terminal`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/1`<br>`description <text>`<br>`end` | `IF-MIB::ifAlias.<ifIndex> = "<text>"` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18`) | `show interfaces GigabitEthernet0/1 description` or SNMP GET of `ifAlias` | |
| Configure access VLAN | `configure terminal`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/1`<br>`switchport mode access`<br>`switchport access vlan 10`<br>`end` | `CISCO-VLAN-MEMBERSHIP-MIB::vmVlan.<ifIndex> = 10` (`1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.68.1.2.2.1.2`), with `vmVlanType.<ifIndex>` set appropriately (`1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.68.1.2.2.1.1`) | `show vlan brief` (parse port-to-VLAN mapping) or SNMP GET of `vmVlan`/`Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid` | This is a genuine Cisco-documented SNMP write path (see `mib-reference.md`) — one of the few non-`ifAdminStatus` cases where SNMP SET is realistic. `switchport mode access` is required first if the port isn't already in access mode; omit if it already is (GUI logic should check current mode via read-back before emitting). |
| Configure trunk allowed-VLANs | `configure terminal`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/1`<br>`switchport mode trunk`<br>`switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30`<br>`end` | No documented SNMP write path for the trunk allowed-VLAN *list* specifically. (`Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticEgressPorts`/`dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts` bitmasks are theoretically the standards-based mechanism, but we found no Cisco-published how-to exercising this for trunk-allowed-list management the way there is for access-VLAN assignment — treat as unconfirmed, not as a working path.) | `show interfaces trunk` (parse allowed/allowed-and-active VLAN lists) | **CLI-only in practice.** GUI must route this through a live CLI session; no SNMP fallback should be offered for this specific action. |
| Enable/disable spanning-tree PortFast on a port | `configure terminal`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/1`<br>`spanning-tree portfast` (or `spanning-tree portfast disable` / `no spanning-tree portfast` to remove) | None found. `BRIDGE-MIB`/`dot1dStp*` objects are read-only in practice on IOS-XE for this kind of per-port STP tuning parameter. | `show spanning-tree interface GigabitEthernet0/1 detail` (look for "Port is in the portfast..." / "edge" state text) or `show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1` for the literal config line | **CLI-only.** Note IOS-XE will print an interactive warning to the terminal when PortFast is enabled on a port that could form a loop — SignalScope's terminal echo must surface that warning text, not swallow it, since it's part of what a human operator would see. |
| Configure LACP port-channel membership | `configure terminal`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/1`<br>`channel-group 1 mode active`<br>`end` | None found — no MIB path for channel-group membership. | `show etherchannel summary` (parse member/bundle state) or `show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1` | **CLI-only.** If `Port-channel1` doesn't already exist, IOS-XE creates it implicitly on the first `channel-group` command — GUI should reflect the new `Port-channel1` interface appearing, sourced from the read-back, not assume it pre-existed. |
| Enable/disable port-security | `configure terminal`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/1`<br>`switchport mode access` (if not already)<br>`switchport port-security`<br>`switchport port-security maximum <n>`<br>`switchport port-security violation {protect\|restrict\|shutdown}`<br>`end` | `CISCO-PORT-SECURITY-MIB` objects (`cpsIfPortSecurityEnable` `1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.315.1.2.1.1.1`, `cpsIfMaxSecureMacAddr`, `cpsIfViolationAction`) are defined `read-write` in the MIB, but **no Cisco-documented SNMP-driven configuration workflow was found** for actually using them this way (see `mib-reference.md`). | `show port-security interface GigabitEthernet0/1` | **Treat as CLI-only despite `read-write` MIB access** — this is the flagged case where trusting `MAX-ACCESS` alone would be wrong. Disabling is `no switchport port-security` (removes the feature from the port entirely, not a toggle). |
| Save / persist configuration | `copy running-config startup-config` (accept default filename prompt) — or non-interactive `write memory` | `CISCO-CONFIG-COPY-MIB::ccCopyTable` row creation with `ccCopySourceFileType = runningConfig(4)`, `ccCopyDestFileType = startupConfig(3)`, `ccCopyEntryRowStatus = createAndGo(4)` (root `1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.96.1.1.1.1`) | `ccCopyState`/`ccCopyEntryRowStatus` polling until the row shows completion (`successState`), or a subsequent CLI `show running-config` vs. stored startup diff | This is Cisco's one thoroughly SNMP-documented write path outside of `ifAdminStatus`/VLAN membership — a legitimate fallback when no CLI session is open. Per `overview.md`'s config-apply model: this operation does *not* change any live behavior (running-config is already in effect) — it only persists it to NVRAM, so the GUI's "Save" affordance for Cisco devices should be labeled/understood as "persist to startup-config," distinct from any notion of "commit my edits." |
| Configure an SNMP community / trap host | `configure terminal`<br>`snmp-server community private RW`<br>`snmp-server host 10.0.0.5 traps public`<br>`snmp-server enable traps snmp linkdown linkup`<br>`end` | None — SNMP cannot configure its own agent (no MIB object writes its own community-string/trap-host config; would be circular). | `show running-config \| section snmp-server` | **CLI-only, structurally** (not just "no documented path" — there is no such object by design). This is also the one config item SignalScope must reach on **first contact** with a device before any SNMP-based read-back is possible at all, so this specific action can never have an SNMP-first flow even in principle. |
